title: Modular admin stencil: runbooks as atomic tasks with safe replay
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Operators frequently run ad-hoc scripts and multi-step runbooks during incidents. We need a light-weight, composable 'stencil' that converts runbook steps and admin snippets into atomic, replayable tasks with typed inputs, dry-run, and automatic telemetry hooks. Goal: provide engineers a small runtime and UX to author, validate, and execute runbook fragments (stencils) that can be chained and re-used across incidents and normal support flows. This ticket implements the core runtime, a task metadata contract, and a minimal web UI to trigger stencils with validation and safe-replay controls. It complements but does not replace the full runbook system; think of it as the atomic primitives library for support automation.
acceptance_criteria: Stencil schema v1 (metadata, inputs, required auth scope, idempotency token) is defined and documented
Runtime can execute 1-step and 3-step stencils with dry-run mode returning simulated outputs
Every stencil execution emits telemetry events (start, step, end, result, error) to existing ops telemetry pipeline
Web UI supports selecting a stencil, filling typed inputs, running dry-run, and executing with an optional reason
Execution is gated by role-based scopes; attempts without proper scope are rejected with audit log entry
implementation_steps: Design stencil JSON schema and idempotency contract (PR to docs/confluence)
Implement lightweight runtime library (Go) with sandboxed shell adapter and test harness
Add telemetry instrumentation and map to ops-metrics events; ensure trace correlation with request id
Create small React admin page in Console with form generator based on stencil schema
Write integration tests (integration-suite) and incident-playbook smoke tests
Create migration plan for existing runbook snippets to stencils and communicate to SREs
risks: Running arbitrary admin snippets could escalate privileges — mitigate via strict RBAC and input validation
Idempotency guarantees are hard if underlying operations are non-idempotent; we require best-effort compensating actions
Telemetry volume could spike; ensure sampling and cost budget rules are applied
Operator UX confusion if stencil semantics differ from existing runbooks — plan communication and training
